description: Design an Adaptive LMS filter in Verilog that takes an input signal and a desired signal, updates filter coefficients based on the LMS algorithm, and outputs the filtered signal.
code:
module adaptive_lms_filter (  
    input clk,  
    input reset,  
    input signed [15:0] x, // input signal  
    input signed [15:0] d, // desired signal  
    output reg signed [15:0] y // output signal  
);  
    parameter N = 5; // number of taps  
    parameter mu = 16'h0001; // step size  
  
    reg signed [15:0] w [0:N-1]; // filter coefficients  
    reg signed [15:0] x_history [0:N-1]; // input history  
    integer i;  
  
    always @(posedge clk or posedge reset) begin  
        if (reset) begin  
            for (i = 0; i < N; i = i + 1) begin  
                w[i] <= 16'h0000; // Initialize coefficients to zero  
            end  
            y <= 16'h0000; // Initialize output to zero  
        end else begin  
            // Shift input history  
            for (i = N-1; i > 0; i = i - 1) begin  
                x_history[i] <= x_history[i-1];  
            end  
            x_history[0] <= x; // Update latest input  
  
            // Calculate output  
            y <= 16'h0000;  
            for (i = 0; i < N; i = i + 1) begin  
                y <= y + (w[i] * x_history[i]);  
            end  
  
            // Update coefficients  
            for (i = 0; i < N; i = i + 1) begin  
                w[i] <= w[i] + (mu * (d - y) * x_history[i]);  
            end  
        end  
    end  
endmodule

);

            clk_out <= 1'b0;

description:
Create a simple 2-bit Branch Predictor. The predictor should use a 2-bit saturating counter to predict the branch outcome (taken or not taken). The states will be:
00 - strongly not taken
01 - weakly not taken
10 - weakly taken
11 - strongly taken

The input will be a branch signal (1 for taken, 0 for not taken) and the output will be the prediction (1 for taken, 0 for not taken). The state will be updated based on the actual branch outcome.
code:
module branch_predictor (
    input clk,
    input reset,
    input branch_taken,
    output reg prediction
);
    reg [1:0] state;

    always @(posedge clk or posedge reset) begin
        if (reset) begin
            state <= 2'b00; // Initialize to strongly not taken
            prediction <= 0;
        end else begin
            prediction <= (state[1] == 1) ? 1 : 0; // Output prediction based on state

            // Update state based on actual branch outcome
            case (state)
                2'b00: state <= branch_taken ? 2'b01 : 2'b00; // 00 -> 01 or stay 00
                2'b01: state <= branch_taken ? 2'b10 : 2'b00; // 01 -> 10 or go back to 00
                2'b10: state <= branch_taken ? 2'b11 : 2'b01; // 10 -> 11 or go back to 01
                2'b11: state <= branch_taken ? 2'b11 : 2'b10; // 11 -> stay 11 or go back to 10
            endcase
        end
    end
endmodule

module bellman_ford #(parameter NUM_NODES = 5) (
    input wire [NUM_NODES*NUM_NODES-1:0] adj_matrix, // adjacency matrix flattened
    input wire [NUM_NODES-1:0] weights, // weight of edges
    input wire [2:0] source, // source node (0 to NUM_NODES-1)
    output reg [NUM_NODES-1:0] distances // distances from source
);

        for (i = 0; i < NUM_NODES; i = i + 1) begin
            distances[i] = (i == source) ? 0 : 8'hFF; // Set inf for other nodes
        end
        
        // Relax edges repeatedly
        for (k = 0; k < NUM_NODES-1; k = k + 1) begin
            for (i = 0; i < NUM_NODES; i = i + 1) begin
                for (j = 0; j < NUM_NODES; j = j + 1) begin
                    if (adj_matrix[i*NUM_NODES + j] && (distances[i] + weights[j] < distances[j])) begin

            end
        end
    end
endmodule

Create a simple ARQ (Automatic Repeat reQuest) error correction system that can resend a message if an error is detected. The system should have a sender that transmits a data bit and a receiver that checks for errors. If an error is detected, the receiver should request the sender to resend the data.

module arq_system (
    input wire clk,
    input wire reset,
    input wire data_in,
    input wire error_detected,
    output reg data_out,
    output reg request_resend
);
    reg [1:0] state;
    
    parameter IDLE = 2'b00,
              SEND = 2'b01,
              WAIT = 2'b10;

    always @(posedge clk or posedge reset) begin
        if (reset) begin
            state <= IDLE;
            data_out <= 0;
            request_resend <= 0;
        end else begin
            case (state)
                IDLE: begin
                    state <= SEND;
                    request_resend <= 0;
                end
                SEND: begin
                    data_out <= data_in;
                    if (error_detected) begin
                        request_resend <= 1;
                        state <= WAIT;
                    end else begin
                        state <= IDLE; // Go back to idle if no error
                    end
                end
                WAIT: begin
                    if (!error_detected) begin
                        request_resend <= 0; // Reset request when error is gone
                        state <= IDLE; // Return to idle
                    end
                end
            endcase
        end
    end
endmodule

    input wire reset,
    input wire modulated_signal,
    input wire reference_freq,

The FFT should be performed synchronously on a clock signal with a start signal to indicate when the computation should begin. The output should be valid when an output ready signal is asserted.
code:
module fft_4point(
    input clk,
    input rst,
    input start,
    input [15:0] x0, // Complex input 0 (real, imag)
    input [15:0] x1, // Complex input 1 (real, imag)
    input [15:0] x2, // Complex input 2 (real, imag)
    input [15:0] x3, // Complex input 3 (real, imag)
    output reg [15:0] y0, // Complex output 0 (real, imag)
    output reg [15:0] y1, // Complex output 1 (real, imag)
    output reg [15:0] y2, // Complex output 2 (real, imag)
    output reg [15:0] y3, // Complex output 3 (real, imag)
    output reg done // Output valid signal
);
    reg [1:0] state;
    reg [15:0] w0, w1, w2, w3; // Twiddle factors
    reg [15:0] temp0, temp1, temp2, temp3; // Temporary storage for FFT calculations

    localparam IDLE = 2'b00;
    localparam COMPUTE = 2'b01;
    localparam DONE = 2'b10;

    always @(posedge clk or posedge rst) begin
        if (rst) begin
            state <= IDLE;
            done <= 0;
        end else begin
            case (state)
                IDLE: begin
                    if (start) begin
                        // Initialize twiddle factors
                        w0 <= 16'h0001; // e^(j*0)
                        w1 <= 16'h0000; // e^(j*pi/2)
                        w2 <= 16'hFFFF; // e^(j*pi)
                        w3 <= 16'h0000; // e^(j*3*pi/2)
                        state <= COMPUTE;
                        done <= 0;
                    end
                end
                COMPUTE: begin
                    // Perform FFT computation here
                    // Using a simple radix-2 decimation-in-time FFT
                    temp0 <= x0 + x2; // FFT computation for output 0
                    temp1 <= x1 + x3; // FFT computation for output 1
                    temp2 <= x0 - x2; // FFT computation for output 2
                    temp3 <= x1 - x3; // FFT computation for output 3

                    y0 <= temp0; // Output 0
                    y1 <= temp1; // Output 1
                    y2 <= temp2; // Output 2
                    y3 <= temp3; // Output 3

                    state <= DONE;
                end
                DONE: begin
                    done <= 1;
                    state <= IDLE;
                end
            endcase
        end
    end
endmodule

Implement a simple combinational logic circuit that calculates the option price using the Black-Scholes model formula. The inputs will be:

- K: Strike price (8 bits)

- r: Risk-free interest rate (8 bits, represented in a fixed-point format)
- sigma: Volatility (8 bits, represented in a fixed-point format)

The output will be the calculated option price (16 bits). The Black-Scholes formula for a European call option price is:
C = S * N(d1) - K * e^(-rT) * N(d2)
where:

module divide_by_2 (
    input wire clk,
    input wire rst,
    input wire in,
    output reg out
);
    always @(posedge clk or posedge rst) begin
        if (rst) begin
            out <= 0;
        end else begin
            out <= in ^ out; // Toggle output on every clock cycle
        end
    end
endmodule

description: Create a Verilog module that implements a non-restoring divider. The module should take two inputs: a dividend and a divisor, both of 8 bits. The output should be the quotient and the remainder, both also 8 bits. The non-restoring division algorithm should be used to perform the division operation.

Design a carrier frequency recovery circuit that takes a modulated input signal and recovers the original frequency signal. The circuit should implement a phase-locked loop (PLL) mechanism to synchronize the output frequency with the input signal's frequency.
code:
module pll_recovery (
    input wire clk,             // Clock signal
    input wire reset,           // Reset signal
    input wire modulated_signal, // Input modulated signal
    output reg recovered_signal   // Recovered frequency output signal
);
    reg [3:0] phase_error;     // Phase error register
    reg [3:0] phase_adjust;     // Phase adjustment amount

    always @(posedge clk or posedge reset) begin
        if (reset) begin
            recovered_signal <= 0;
            phase_error <= 0;
            phase_adjust <= 0;
        end else begin
            // Simple PLL mechanism
            phase_error <= modulated_signal ^ recovered_signal; // Calculate phase error
            phase_adjust <= phase_error; // Update phase adjustment
            recovered_signal <= recovered_signal + phase_adjust; // Adjust output signal
        end
    end
endmodule

description: Create a Verilog module that implements a second-order Butterworth low-pass filter. The filter should take a 4-bit signed input `x` and produce a 4-bit signed output `y`. The filter coefficients are fixed and should be designed to provide a cutoff frequency of approximately 1 kHz when sampled at 10 kHz. The filter should utilize a state machine to process the input data and produce the output.

Design a clock gating circuit in Verilog. The circuit should enable or disable a clock signal based on a control signal. When the control signal is high, the clock should be gated (enabled), and when the control signal is low, the clock should be disabled (hold the last value). Implement a D flip-flop that captures the input data when the gated clock is enabled.
code:
module clock_gating (
    input wire clk,
    input wire enable,
    input wire d,
    output reg q
);
    reg gated_clk;

    always @(*) begin
        gated_clk = clk & enable; // Clock gating logic
    end

    always @(posedge gated_clk) begin
        q <= d; // D flip-flop behavior
    end
endmodule

description: Design a 16-bit timer that counts up from 0 to a specified maximum value (MAX). The timer should have a clock input (clk), a reset input (rst), and a load input (load) to load a new value into the timer. When the load signal is active, the timer should take the value from a 16-bit input (data_in). When reset is active, the timer should reset to 0. When counting, the timer increments on each clock cycle until it reaches MAX, where it should hold that value. The timer should have a flag output (done) that goes high when the timer has reached MAX.

Create a Verilog module that implements a simple neuron which takes 3 inputs (x1, x2, x3) and produces an output (y). The output is calculated using the following formula:  
y = w1*x1 + w2*x2 + w3*x3 + b  
Where w1 = 2, w2 = -1, w3 = 3, and b = 1.  
The module should be synthesized and tested for different input combinations.

Create a combinational logic circuit that implements a simple decision tree with the following structure:
- Input: 3-bit binary number (X[2:0])
- Decision: 
  - If X[2] == 0 and X[1] == 0, output 0
  - If X[2] == 0 and X[1] == 1, output 1
  - If X[2] == 1 and X[1] == 0, output 2
  - If X[2] == 1 and X[1] == 1, output 3
- The output should be a 2-bit binary number (Y[1:0]).
code:
module decision_tree (
    input  [2:0] X,
    output reg [1:0] Y
);
    always @* begin
        case ({X[2], X[1]})
            2'b00: Y = 2'b00; // case: X[2] == 0, X[1] == 0
            2'b01: Y = 2'b01; // case: X[2] == 0, X[1] == 1
            2'b10: Y = 2'b10; // case: X[2] == 1, X[1] == 0
            2'b11: Y = 2'b11; // case: X[2] == 1, X[1] == 1
            default: Y = 2'b00; // default case
        endcase
    end
endmodule

description:
Design a 4-bit SRAM cell that can store a 4-bit value. The SRAM cell should have the following inputs and outputs:
- Inputs: `address` (2 bits), `data_in` (4 bits), `write_enable` (1 bit), and `read_enable` (1 bit).
- Outputs: `data_out` (4 bits) which should output the stored value when read, and should be valid only when `read_enable` is high.

The SRAM should be able to store 4 different 4-bit values at different addresses. When `write_enable` is high, the input data should be stored at the specified address. When `read_enable` is high, the data from the specified address should be output.
code:
module sram_cell (
    input [1:0] address,
    input [3:0] data_in,
    input write_enable,
    input read_enable,
    output reg [3:0] data_out
);

    reg [3:0] memory [3:0]; // 4-bit memory with 4 addresses

    always @(posedge write_enable) begin
        if (write_enable) begin
            memory[address] <= data_in;
        end
    end

    always @(posedge read_enable) begin
        if (read_enable) begin
            data_out <= memory[address];
        end
    end
endmodule

description: Implement a simplified version of the ChaCha20 stream cipher core. The design must include the key schedule and the quarter-round function used in the ChaCha20 algorithm. The state consists of 16 32-bit words, initialized with a constant, the key, and a nonce. Your task is to design the state update mechanism to produce the next output block based on the current state and key schedule.

Design a 4-bit down counter that counts from a specified value down to zero. The counter should have a clock input, a reset input, and a load input. When the reset input is asserted, the counter should be reset to the specified initial value. When the load input is asserted, the counter should load a new value. The counter should decrement its value on each clock cycle.
code:
module down_counter (  
    input clk,  
    input reset,  
    input load,  
    input [3:0] load_value,  
    output reg [3:0] count  
);  
    always @(posedge clk or posedge reset) begin  
        if (reset) begin  
            count <= load_value;  
        end else if (load) begin  
            count <= load_value;  
        end else if (count > 0) begin  
            count <= count - 1;  
        end  
    end  
endmodule

description: Design a SPI (Serial Peripheral Interface) controller that can operate in Master mode. The controller should handle the clock generation, chip select, and data transmission. The master device will send data to a slave device on a rising edge of the SPI clock and expect to receive data on the falling edge. The controller should allow for a configurable number of bits to be transmitted (8, 16, or 32 bits).

Design a simple QAM modulator that takes in 2 bits of input (representing the in-phase and quadrature components) and outputs a 4-bit representation of the QAM signal. The mapping is as follows:
00 -> 0000
01 -> 0001
10 -> 0010

Create an SR latch using D flip-flops. The latch should have two inputs S (Set) and R (Reset), and one output Q. The output Q should be high when S is high and R is low, and it should reset to low when R is high regardless of S.

Design a 4-bit Wallace tree multiplier in Verilog. The module should take two 4-bit unsigned inputs and output an 8-bit unsigned product. The Wallace tree multiplier should consist of partial product generation, reduction using carry save adders, and final addition to produce the result.

Create a clock gating circuit that controls the clock signal of a flip-flop based on an enable signal. The flip-flop should hold its value when the enable signal is low, and update its value on the rising edge of the clock when the enable signal is high.
code:

);

        end
    end
endmodule

description: Design a 128-bit AES encryption module. The module should take a 128-bit plaintext and a 128-bit key as inputs and produce a 128-bit ciphertext output. Additionally, it should support an enable signal to control the start of the encryption process. The module should also have a reset signal to clear the internal state.

Create a simple PCIe interface receiver module that accepts a 32-bit data input signal and an associated 3-bit address signal. The receiver should latch the data and address on a rising edge of a clock signal when a valid signal is asserted. The module should output the latched data and address when requested by an output enable signal.

description: Design an 8-bit deserializer that converts an 8-bit serial input into an 8-bit parallel output. The deserializer should accept one bit of data on each clock cycle and output the 8 bits once all bits have been received. There should be a reset signal that initializes the deserializer, and a valid signal that indicates when the output is ready.

Design a simple reset controller that has a reset signal (reset) and a clock signal (clk). When reset is high, the output (out) should be set to 0. Otherwise, on the rising edge of the clock, the output should increment by 1, and it should wrap around when it reaches 8 (i.e., when out is 7, the next increment should set it back to 0).
code:
module reset_controller(
    input wire clk,
    input wire reset,
    output reg [2:0] out
);
    always @(posedge clk or posedge reset) begin
        if (reset) begin
            out <= 3'b000; // Reset output to 0
        end else begin
            out <= out + 1; // Increment output
            if (out == 3'b111) begin
                out <= 3'b000; // Wrap around when reaching 8
            end
        end
    end
endmodule

description: Design a Verilog module that evaluates a quadratic polynomial of the form P(x) = ax^2 + bx + c, where a, b, and c are 8-bit signed coefficients and x is a 4-bit unsigned input. The output should be a 16-bit signed result of the polynomial evaluation.

Design a simple SATA controller state machine that manages the states of a SATA device. The controller should have the following states: IDLE, ACTIVE, and ERROR. The controller should transition from IDLE to ACTIVE on a 'start' signal and from ACTIVE to IDLE on a 'stop' signal. The controller should enter ERROR state if an 'error' signal is asserted while in ACTIVE state. The output of the controller should indicate the current state as a 2-bit binary value.

Design a simple PCIe endpoint controller that manages read requests. The controller should accept incoming read requests and generate the appropriate response after a fixed delay. The controller has the following signals: `req` (input), `addr` (input), `data_out` (output), and `ack` (output). The `ack` signal should be asserted after a delay of 4 clock cycles when a read request is received. The `data_out` should be equal to the address received for the read request.

Design a data forwarding unit that resolves data hazards in a pipelined processor. The unit takes three 5-bit inputs: `src1`, `src2` (the source registers), and `dest` (the destination register). The output should be a 2-bit signal `forward` which indicates whether the data should be forwarded from one of the two source registers or not. The forwarding logic is defined as follows:
- If `src1` matches `dest`, forward from the destination (output `01`).
- If `src2` matches `dest`, forward from the destination (output `10`).
- If neither matches, no forwarding is needed (output `00`).
code:
module data_forwarding (
    input [4:0] src1,
    input [4:0] src2,
    input [4:0] dest,
    output reg [1:0] forward
);

always @(*) begin
    if (src1 == dest) begin
        forward = 2'b01; // Forward from dest to src1
    end else if (src2 == dest) begin
        forward = 2'b10; // Forward from dest to src2
    end else begin
        forward = 2'b00; // No forwarding
    end
end

endmodule

description: Design a simple Kalman filter for sensor fusion in Verilog. The filter should estimate the state of a dynamic system based on noisy measurements. The design will consist of state prediction and measurement update steps. The inputs to the filter will be a control input and a measurement input, and the outputs will be the estimated state and error covariance.

Design a 16-bit up counter with enable and reset inputs. The counter should increment on every clock cycle when the enable signal is high. If the reset signal is high, the counter should reset to zero. The counter should also have a maximum value of 65535 (0xFFFF) and wrap around to 0 after reaching this maximum.
code:
module counter_16bit (
    input clk,
    input reset,
    input enable,
    output reg [15:0] count
);
    
    always @(posedge clk or posedge reset) begin
        if (reset) begin
            count <= 16'b0;
        end else if (enable) begin
            if (count == 16'hFFFF) begin
                count <= 16'b0;
            end else begin
                count <= count + 1;
            end
        end
    end
endmodule

description: Design an Adaptive LMS (Least Mean Squares) filter in Verilog. The filter should have the following inputs: a signal input (x), a desired signal (d), a step size (mu), and a clock signal (clk). The filter should output the filter output (y) and the error signal (e), where e = d - y. The filter should adapt its coefficients based on the LMS algorithm.

Design a Verilog module for a simplified SLAM system that estimates the position of a robot based on sensor inputs and maintains a simple map of the environment. The module should have a state machine to process sensor data and update the robot's position. The inputs are sensor readings (e.g., distance measurements) and the outputs are the updated position coordinates (x, y) of the robot.

Design a Deadbeat controller in Verilog that takes a 3-bit input representing the current state and produces a 3-bit output that drives the system to a desired state in a single clock cycle. The desired state is also a 3-bit value. The control logic will be designed to immediately correct the output to match the desired state based on the input state.

Design a simple pitch detection module that takes a 4-bit binary input representing the frequency of a tone and outputs a signal indicating whether the frequency is within a specified range (e.g., 4'b1000 to 4'b1100). The output should be '1' if the input frequency is within the range and '0' otherwise. The module should also include a reset signal to initialize the output to '0'.
Create a 4-input NAND gate using Verilog. The output should be high when at least one of the inputs is low. Provide a testbench that reads inputs and expected outputs from a file.
Design a 2-bit multiplier in Verilog that takes two 2-bit inputs and produces a 4-bit output. The output should be the product of the two input values.

Design a simple sliding window protocol for data transmission. The protocol should manage the sender's window size, allowing the sender to transmit a limited number of frames before waiting for an acknowledgment. Implement the sender's state machine where the sender can send data, receive acknowledgments, and handle timeouts.

Design a UART transmitter module in Verilog that takes an 8-bit data input, a start bit, a stop bit, and a clock signal. The module should output the serial data stream, which includes the start bit, the data bits (LSB first), and the stop bit. The module should operate at a fixed baud rate defined by a parameter. The transmitter should also handle data ready signals to indicate when new data is available for transmission.

Design a temperature-based shutdown system that monitors the temperature of a device. If the temperature exceeds a set threshold, the system will trigger a shutdown signal. The device's temperature can be updated periodically, and the system should retain the last known temperature until a new one is received. The threshold value will be provided as an input. The system should also have an enable signal to start monitoring.
code:
module temperature_shutdown (
    input clk,
    input rst_n,
    input enable,
    input [7:0] temperature, // 8-bit temperature input
    input [7:0] threshold,   // 8-bit threshold input
    output reg shutdown       // shutdown signal
);

reg [7:0] last_temperature;

always @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
    if (!rst_n) begin
        last_temperature <= 8'b0;
        shutdown <= 1'b0;
    end else if (enable) begin
        last_temperature <= temperature; // Update last known temperature
        if (last_temperature > threshold) begin
            shutdown <= 1'b1; // Trigger shutdown if temperature exceeds threshold
        end else begin
            shutdown <= 1'b0; // Otherwise, do not shutdown
        end
    end
end

endmodule

description: Design an HMAC (Hash-based Message Authentication Code) module that takes a key and a message as inputs and produces a tag output. The HMAC should use a simple XOR operation for this problem, followed by a simple shift and modulus operation to simulate a hash function. The inputs should be 64 bits each, and the output should be 64 bits. The key and message will be provided as inputs in the testbench.

Design a 4-bit Parallel-in Serial-out (PISO) shift register. The module should have inputs for clock, load, a 4-bit parallel input, and a serial output. When the load signal is high, the parallel data should be loaded into the shift register. On each clock pulse, if the load signal is low, the data should shift out serially. The output should be valid for one clock cycle after it is shifted out.
code:
module PISO #(
    parameter WIDTH = 4
)(
    input clk,
    input load,
    input [WIDTH-1:0] parallel_in,
    output reg serial_out
);
    reg [WIDTH-1:0] shift_reg;

    always @(posedge clk) begin
        if (load) begin
            shift_reg <= parallel_in;  // Load parallel data
        end else begin
            serial_out <= shift_reg[WIDTH-1]; // Shift out the MSB
            shift_reg <= {shift_reg[WIDTH-2:0], 1'b0}; // Shift left
        end
    end
endmodule

description: Design a simple MD5-like hash function that takes a 128-bit input and produces a 32-bit output. The hash should be computed by taking the input, splitting it into four 32-bit blocks, and then performing a simple XOR and addition operation on these blocks to produce the final hash value.

Design a 16-bit shift register with parallel load capability. The shift register should have a clock input, a reset input, a load input, and a 16-bit input data bus. When the load input is high, the shift register should load the input data. When the load input is low, on each clock cycle, the contents of the register should shift right by one bit. The most significant bit (MSB) should be filled with 0 during shifting. The shift register should also be reset to 0 when the reset input is high.
code:
module shift_register(
    input clk,
    input reset,
    input load,
    input [15:0] data_in,
    output reg [15:0] q
);

always @(posedge clk or posedge reset) begin
    if (reset) begin
        q <= 16'b0;
    end else if (load) begin
        q <= data_in;
    end else begin
        q <= {1'b0, q[15:1]}; // Shift right and fill MSB with 0
    end
end

endmodule

Design a simple hash table with a fixed size of 16 entries. The hash table will support two operations: 
1. Insertion of a key-value pair into the table. 
2. Retrieval of a value by its key. The hash function will compute an index based on the key modulo the size of the hash table. If a collision occurs during insertion, the new value will overwrite the existing one. The keys will be 8 bits wide and the values will be 8 bits wide as well. The design should handle up to 5 key-value pairs.

Design a Verilog module that implements a 16-QAM (Quadrature Amplitude Modulation) encoder. The module should take a 4-bit input representing the symbol to be encoded and produce two outputs (I and Q), each being a 2-bit value corresponding to the in-phase (I) and quadrature (Q) components of the modulation. The mapping for 16-QAM should be as follows:

- 0001            | 00         | 01
- 0010            | 00         | 10
- 0011            | 00         | 11
- 0100            | 01         | 00
- 0101            | 01         | 01
- 0110            | 01         | 10
- 0111            | 01         | 11
- 1000            | 10         | 00
- 1001            | 10         | 01
- 1010            | 10         | 10
- 1011            | 10         | 11
- 1100            | 11         | 00
- 1101            | 11         | 01

    output reg [1:0] I,

);

            4'b0110: begin I = 2'b01; Q = 2'b10; end
            4'b0111: begin I = 2'b01; Q = 2'b11; end
            4'b1000: begin I = 2'b10; Q = 2'b00; end
            4'b1001: begin I = 2'b10; Q = 2'b01; end
            4'b1010: begin I = 2'b10; Q = 2'b10; end
            4'b1011: begin I = 2'b10; Q = 2'b11; end
            4'b1100: begin I = 2'b11; Q = 2'b00; end
            4'b1101: begin I = 2'b11; Q = 2'b01; end
            4'b1110: begin I = 2'b11; Q = 2'b10; end
            4'b1111: begin I = 2'b11; Q = 2'b11; end

description: Design a simple Ethernet MAC controller state machine that handles the basic operations of receiving and transmitting data frames. The state machine should have two states: IDLE and TRANSMIT. When a transmit signal is asserted, the state machine enters the TRANSMIT state, sends out a frame, and then returns to the IDLE state. The state machine should also respond to a reset signal, which forces it back to the IDLE state.

Design a 2-to-4 decoder with an enable input. The decoder should take 2 input bits and produce 4 output lines. If the enable input is low, all output lines should be low. If the enable input is high, the output corresponding to the binary value of the 2 input bits should be high, while all other output lines should be low.

Design a simple Low Dropout Regulator (LDO) control logic using Verilog. The LDO should have an enable input, a voltage reference input, and a feedback voltage input. The output should be a control signal that enables or disables the regulator based on the feedback voltage compared to the reference voltage.
code:
module ldo_regulator (
    input wire enable,          // Enable signal for LDO
    input wire [7:0] v_ref,    // Reference voltage input
    input wire [7:0] v_fb,     // Feedback voltage input
    output reg control          // Control output signal
);

always @(*) begin
    if (enable) begin
        if (v_fb < v_ref) begin
            control = 1; // Enable LDO
        end else begin
            control = 0; // Disable LDO
        end
    end else begin
        control = 0; // Disable LDO if not enabled
    end
end

endmodule

description: Design a combinational logic circuit that implements a simplified Hough Transform for detecting straight lines in a binary image. The circuit should take a binary image represented by an 8x8 array as input and output the parameters (r, θ) of the detected lines. The parameters should be encoded in a way that r is a 6-bit value and θ is a 4-bit value. Assume the maximum possible value for r is 63 and for θ is 15 (representing angles from 0 to 180 degrees).

Design a deadbeat controller in Verilog that takes a 4-bit input representing the current state of a system and a 4-bit input representing the desired state. The controller should compute the control action needed to transition the current state to the desired state in one clock cycle. The output should be a 4-bit control signal. Implement this logic in Verilog.
code:
module deadbeat_controller (
    input wire clk,
    input wire [3:0] current_state,
    input wire [3:0] desired_state,
    output reg [3:0] control_signal
);
    always @(posedge clk) begin
        control_signal <= desired_state - current_state; // Compute control signal
    end
endmodule

description: Design an 8-bit shift register with serial input and output. The shift register should have a clock input and a reset input. On the rising edge of the clock, if the reset is low, the shift register should shift to the right and load a new bit from the serial input. If reset is high, the shift register should be cleared to zero.
code:
module shift_register (  
    input clk,  
    input reset,  
    input serial_in,  
    output reg [7:0] parallel_out  
);  
  
    always @(posedge clk or posedge reset) begin  
        if (reset) begin  
            parallel_out <= 8'b00000000;  
        end else begin  
            parallel_out <= {parallel_out[6:0], serial_in};  
        end  
    end  
endmodule

description: Design a 4-bit Parallel-in Serial-out (PISO) shift register. The shift register should accept a 4-bit parallel input and shift out the bits serially on a clock edge. There should be a load signal to load the parallel data into the register, and a serial output signal to output the shifted bits.
code:
module PISO (
    input wire clk,
    input wire load,
    input wire [3:0] parallel_in,
    output reg serial_out
);
    reg [3:0] shift_reg;
    reg [1:0] count; // to count the number of bits shifted out

    always @(posedge clk) begin
        if (load) begin
            shift_reg <= parallel_in; // Load parallel data into the shift register
            count <= 2'b00; // Reset count
        end else if (count < 2'b11) begin
            serial_out <= shift_reg[3]; // Output the MSB
            shift_reg <= {shift_reg[2:0], 1'b0}; // Shift left
            count <= count + 1; // Increment count
        end
